title: Pseudorandomness of Iterated Three-Wire Permutations
summary: The broader, weaker three-wire reversible-circuit conjecture asks whether polynomially many random local-permutation steps yield a pseudorandom permutation.

formal_statement.body: Let $P:\{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^n$ be the randomized permutation process that chooses three random wires and applies a uniformly random permutation to those wires. The unresolved conjecture asks whether there is a polynomial $p$ such that the iterated process $P^{p(n)}$ is a pseudorandom permutation. This is the broader random three-wire reversible-circuit question; it is weaker than the preceding restricted conjectures, so refuting it would also refute those conjectures.

scope.domain: Pseudorandomness and probabilistic mixing of random three-wire reversible permutations on n-bit strings.
parameters: p: polynomial whose value at n determines the number of iterations
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether there exists a polynomial p such that iterating the randomized process p(n) times yields a pseudorandom permutation.

citations.label: When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness

progress.summary: The source explicitly states this as Conjecture 7 and presents it as broader and weaker than Conjectures 3–6. The conjecture remains unresolved, and refuting it would also refute those restricted conjectures.
